ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio between dominant low-intensity black/dark grey surface area (approx. 85%) and localized high-intensity white/light grey regions (approx. 15%) primarily at the distal tips and along the trailing edge.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary surface consists of a continuous dark pigmentation field. High-intensity white mottling and solid banding is concentrated at the distal tips of both lobes. A prominent, low-intensity circular dark spot is visible in the mid-section of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, narrow V-shaped central depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 42 degrees and a significant depth relative to the lobe width.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations throughout. Noted alternating pixel-amplitude peaks and valleys, with a significant jagged notch located on the inner trailing edge of the right lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave trajectory originating from the median notch, transitioning to a sharp convex curve at the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density clusters of circular, high-contrast white pixel groups (barnacles) localized at the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint, vertical-oriented linear pixel disruptions of light grey intensity distributed across the central area of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Massive barnacle colonization at both lobe extremities. A large, distinct circular pigmentation anomaly on the left lobe. A deep, irregular semicircular indentation on the trailing edge of the right lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: A highly unique, isolated circular dark spot positioned in the upper-left quadrant of the fluke surface, contrasting sharply with the surrounding grey-mottled texture.
